chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about making the absconding slave suffer humiliation. He said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.الآبِق: The absconding slave who runs away from his master
key_terms.الضَّالَّة: The stray animal or lost property
key_terms.جَعْل: A fixed sum, fine, or monetary valuation
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on imposing a fine on an absconding slave?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms the permissibility of setting a monetary value (ju'l) for an absconding slave (al-abiq) and a stray animal (al-dhallah), reflecting the practical legal norms of early Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding property rights and compensation mechanisms, aligning with the broader principles of maintaining social order and economic stability in the community.
